task1.title: The manufacturing process for making sugar from sugar cane
task1.prompt: The diagram below shows the manufacturing process for making sugar from sugar cane.

chartDesc.title: How sugar is produced from sugar cane

stages.label: Growing (12–18 months)
stages.detail: Sugar canes are grown over a period of 12 to 18 months.

stages.label: Harvesting
stages.detail: Sugar canes are harvested either mechanically using an agricultural vehicle or manually by a worker.

stages.label: Crushing
stages.detail: Harvested sugar canes are crushed in a machine to extract juice.

stages.label: Purifying juice
stages.detail: Extracted juice is passed through a limestone filter to be purified.

stages.label: Evaporator (juice becomes syrup)
stages.detail: Purified juice is heated in an evaporator to transform it into syrup.

stages.label: Centrifuge (separates sugar crystals from syrup)
stages.detail: Syrup is spun in a centrifuge to separate sugar crystals from syrup.

stages.label: Drying and cooling
stages.detail: Sugar crystals are dried and cooled to result in finished sugar.

chartDesc.overview: The linear manufacturing process contains 7 numbered steps, starting with growing sugar cane over 12–18 months and finishing with drying and cooling to yield final sugar.
keyFeatures: Linear process consisting of 7 distinct steps numbered from 1 to 7.
Stage 2 (Harvesting) shows two optional methods: mechanical harvesting with a machine and manual harvesting by hand.
Key equipment/materials labeled include sugar canes, juice, limestone filter, evaporator with heat source, centrifuge, and final sugar.
